p:cNvPr.descr: Adenine and guanine are at the top and labeled "purines" below; the remainder are on the bottom and are labeled "pyrimidines" below. Adenine and guanine both have structures containing both a 6-sided ring and a 5-sided ring bonded together. For adenine, on the left, the 6-sided ring begins with the apical carbon. It bonds up to NH2, double bonds down and left to N, which bonds down to CH, which bonds down and right to N. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C, and bonds up and right to the initial C. The 5-sided ring is bonded to the right. Its apical N double bonds down and right to CH, which bonds down to NH, which bonds left to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to the initial N. To the right, the structure of guanine is shown. It is similar to adenine, but has a double bonded O above the top carbon in the 6-sided ring, and the C at the lower left bonds down and left to NH2.
